claims.claim: 1. Settings live in Jetpack DataStore (Preferences or Proto, and the file name).

evidence.quote: private val prefs by lazy { context.getSharedPreferences(PREFS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE) }

claims.claim: 2. Every settings key with its type and default.
3. Any setting syncs between devices (report zero hits if none).

evidence.quote: Deliberately not part of the sync path (§15.2): a phone and a tablet can legitimately want
/** Used only by FullBackupManager — settings are never part of routine sync. */

claims.claim: 4. The sync folder location is a setting; how it is stored (SAF tree URI or path).

evidence.quote: Read-side access to the persisted SAF tree URI — the one folder the person picked to hold both

claims.claim: 5. Settings are included in export or backup.

missed.fact: Settings are split across two stores: Preferences DataStore 'app_settings' (5 keys) and a separate SharedPreferences file 'sync_export' holding the sync-root SAF tree URI under 'tree_uri'. The map's 'one DataStore' claim misses the second store; it is a merge-relevant identity/location store.

The sync-root tree URI is NOT in the backup envelope (FullBackupEnvelope has only schemaVersion, exportedAtEpochMillis, reminders, settings), so a restore never carries the folder. It is device-local, tied to a persisted SAF permission grant, and re-verified on every call; a stored URI without a live write grant returns null.
The one sync folder is shared by per-reminder sync files (reminders/) and the manual full backups written at its root, so it is a single grant serving both.
nagRepeatIntervalMinutes is clamped to 1..30 on READ, so a restored backup value outside that range is pulled to the nearest end. A merge must keep the clamp.
Restore is a full overwrite: restoreFrom calls update { restored }, which writes every field, including hasRequestedBatteryOptExemption, which is a per-device first-run flag and not a preference.

defaultMode and defaultSkinId are plain Strings with no enum. appThemeSkinId is parsed elsewhere by AppTheme.fromStorageKey with a Bark fallback, and the legacy key 'neutral_shell' (written by v1.11–v1.15) is tolerated.
Writing a changed appThemeSkinId triggers WidgetRefresher.refreshAll, so the settings write path has a side effect outside the store. Only a theme change triggers it.
A DataStore IOException is swallowed into emptyPreferences (defaults), so a corrupt file reads as defaults.
The platform backup is disabled: android:allowBackup is false, and a dataExtractionRules XML exists for device-to-device transfer. The only backup route is the app's own manual JSON export.
Stale *.bak-20260926 copies of SyncRootStore, SyncCoordinator and the manifest exist under the source tree. They were ignored.

absence_probes.pattern: DataStore|getSharedPreferences in *.kt/*.kts/*.toml (excluding tests and comments): Proto DataStore (protoDataStore/dataStore(fileName, serializer))
